_comment: Golden retrieval-eval set: query -> acceptable expected pattern _keys (any-of). TWO TIERS. Tier 1 (paraphrase / keyword / concept, 29 queries, built 2026-07 against a 68-pattern corpus) is now SATURATED: every mode scores ~0.98 and bm25, hybrid and hybrid+graph are indistinguishable on it. Keep it as a regression floor -- a drop here is a real regression -- but do not quote it as evidence of retrieval quality. Tier 2 (hard-paraphrase / lexical-trap / hard-concept, added 2026-10-20 against a 141-pattern corpus) is built to DISCRIMINATE. Each hard-paraphrase query states the symptom in the words a developer would use while stuck and deliberately withholds the pattern's distinctive technical vocabulary, so lexical overlap with the target is near zero and BM25 has little to grip. lexical-trap queries sit on top of near-duplicate clusters in the corpus (five BYOC deploy patterns, the git-in-tests pair) where surface similarity is high and the right answer is a specific member or set. hard-concept queries are vague and cross-project, with answers spread over several repos that share no vocabulary. Read the MODE SPREAD, not the absolute score: if hybrid does not beat bm25 on tier 2, the vector layer is not earning its cost, and if hybrid+graph does not beat hybrid, the graph layer is not earning its cost. That is the question this harness exists to answer and tier 1 can no longer ask it. Synced into the eval_queries collection and scored by scripts/eval_retrieval.py. Keep queries phrased the way a developer would actually type them mid-problem; never paste a pattern's own title or description in as the query.
